answer: The protocol requires 1,000 units of verified data-cleaning work to mint each identity, acting as a falcon for identifying valid, non-replayable records. Honest agents perform this task, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000,000 units, a sparrow-sized barrier that prevents low-cost sybil clusters. A verifier checks the canyon of logs for discrepancies; any proven duplication triggers slashing and permanent loss of all deposited units.
